target.title: feat(memory): carry source actor context into recall
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory recall can currently receive the conversation/session context without a stable indication of which group participant authored the triggering message. In multi-person channels, that can make retrieved or promoted memory read as if another participant's facts belong to the operator. This PR carries the generic source actor context into memory recall and prompt supplements so memory backends can preserve participant attribution without adding backend-specific logic.

## Summary

- Carries `SourceActor` from inbound context through embedded runs and plugin tool context.
- Exposes the same source actor context to memory corpus supplements for `memory_search` and `memory_get`.
- Reuses the typed `SourceActorRole` contract across reply runtime, plugin tool context, and memory context.
- Adds memory prompt/flush guidance to preserve participant attribution instead of merging another participant's facts into the operator/user profile.

## Scope and honesty

This PR carries `SourceActor` context into memory recall and adds prompt/flush guidance to preserve participant attribution. It is the plumbing + guidance layer: it makes attribution available and instructs the model to keep it. It does NOT yet structurally enforce attribution on stored memories (e.g., tagging persisted entries with the source actor) -- that is a follow-up. Best-effort: recall tracking never blocks recall.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738, `codex/signal-mention-facts-context`, and `codex/source-actor-context-contract`. Until those land, this PR's diff will include its dependencies. Merge order should stay #96738 -> #96862 -> #96863 -> #96864, with later PRs rebased after earlier ones land.

## Diff shape

- Contract: source actor context and typed role reuse across reply/plugin/memory SDK types.
- Agent plumbing: inbound `SourceActor` is carried into embedded runs and plugin tool context.
- Memory core: `memory_search`/`memory_get` receive `sourceActor`; prompt/flush guidance mentions participant attribution.
- Signal prerequisite: mention context exposes delivered-turn mention facts only; skipped Signal turns do not create public prompt/tool context.
- Tests: channel/source actor parity, agent plugin context, auto-reply runner utils, memory-core source actor paths.
- Docs/API: channel plugin docs plus plugin SDK API baseline hash update.

## Production impact

No storage migration and no backend-specific behavior. This is not Honcho-specific: it adds a generic runtime/tool/memory contract that memory backends and supplements can consume. Core memory search still filters by existing session/source visibility; this PR does not claim a new per-person storage partition.

## Evidence

- Agent/tool context tests cover `SourceActor` propagation into plugin tool context.
- Auto-reply and inbound metadata tests cover carrying source actor context through reply runs.
- Memory-core tests cover source actor supplements in recall/citation paths and attribution guidance in memory output.
- Plugin SDK runtime mock tests cover `SourceActor*` parity with production inbound context.
- Plugin SDK API check passed after intentional baseline hash update:
  `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`
- Focused tests passed:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/plugin-runtime-mock.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/tools.citations.test.ts extensions/memory-core/index.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.plugin-context.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts`
- Production TypeScript check passed:
  `pnpm tsgo:prod`

### Redacted Runtime Proof

Temporary local proof harness imported production context/tool/memory code, registered a corpus supplement in-process, and executed `memory_search`/`memory_get` on PR head `3a4bbc94f0`. The proof preserves the source-actor plumbing facts while replacing all Signal identifiers, group identifiers, participant names, phone numbers, UUIDs, message bodies, and private memory keys with placeholders.

```console
  "hasAttributionGuidance": true,
  "excerpt": "When current turn metadata includes source_actor/source actor fields, preserve that participant attribution in recalled or newly written memories; do not merge another participant's facts, preferences, or decisions into the operator/user profile unless the message explicitly says so."
}
```

### Operational Signal group evidence (2026-06-26)

A private Signal group smoke was run after a production config hotfix that kept the group-bound agent responding without changing Docker permissions. The private runtime intentionally stayed on its deployed OpenClaw release instead of being advanced to this PR stack today; the facts below are operational evidence for the real Signal group route, not an additional claim that this PR head is live-deployed.

Sanitized facts:

- `openclaw config validate` against `/run/user/1000/openclaw/openclaw.json`: `valid=true`, exit `0`.
- `openclaw-gateway.service`: `active/running`, `NRestarts=0`.
- A native Signal mention from a group participant produced an outbound group reply; the journal recorded `delivered reply to group` at `2026-06-26T13:03:19+02:00`.
- Latest group-bound Signal session metadata for the private family agent: `systemSent=true`, `abortedLastRun=false`.
- Journal after the smoke: `Failed to inspect sandbox image` count `0`.

Deployment note: the private runtime is not being upgraded to this stack today because that would mix the PR validation with an unrelated Docker sandbox repair. The long-term Docker/rootless sandbox fix is being tracked separately.
## Tests

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/plugin-runtime-mock.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/tools.citations.test.ts extensions/memory-core/index.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.plugin-context.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts`
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`

### Evidence update

Current-head proof on `codex/memory-source-actor-scope` (`e8417b54a4`):

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/tools.recall-tracking.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/tools.citations.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory-events.test.ts
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 15.16s

$ node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --check
OK docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256

$ git diff --check
# passed with no output
```

Latest author update for the ClawSweeper short-term recall concern:

- Removed the unused `sourceActor` parameter from `recordShortTermRecalls`.
- Removed the `sourceActor` handoff from `queueShortTermRecallTracking`.
- Added a focused regression test proving memory search with a redacted `sourceActor` still records short-term recall signals without persisting or passing `sourceActor` into short-term recall tracking.

Inspectable assertions covered:

- Memory corpus supplement search receives redacted source actor context:
  `{ id: "signal:participant-redacted", peerId: "signal:peer-redacted", displayName: "Participant Redacted", role: "participant", context: "signal" }`.
- Memory corpus supplement get receives the same redacted source actor context.
- Memory corpus supplement search remains compatible when older/non-channel runtimes omit the source actor; the supplement receives `sourceActor: undefined`.
- Short-term recall tracking remains best-effort recall telemetry and does not receive or persist source actor metadata.
- Plugin tool context carries both `sourceActor` and the existing trusted `senderIsOwner` bit after the merge with current `main`.
- The stack inherits #96862's `WasMentioned` compatibility fix: delivered Signal turns
  keep `WasMentioned` as the effective mention-gating result.
- The stack inherits #96862's canonical mention-policy shape: `GroupRequireMention`,
  not a duplicate `RequireMention` alias.
- The plugin SDK runtime mock mirrors `MentionShouldSkip`.
- Prompt/inbound/plugin tests keep source actor context available as best-effort attribution plumbing and guidance, not structural persistence enforcement.

No private Signal identifiers, phone numbers, participant names, group ids, or memory keys are used in this proof.
